card.text: Explore Io in 3D with cssEarth. Inspect Voyager and Galileo imagery of Jupiter’s volcanic moon and its orbit around Jupiter.

introduction.text: Io is Jupiter’s volcanic moon. Tidal heating drives hundreds of volcanoes, continually renewing its sulfur-rich surface.

normal.title: Global image mosaic
normal.summary: Source detail ranges from 1 to 10 km per pixel. Photographed shadows remain; the gray grid marks missing imagery.

enhanced.title: False-color mosaic
enhanced.summary: Infrared, green and violet ratios add color to monochrome detail. Interpolated polar color is withheld from this view.

geology.title: Global geologic map
geology.summary: Fourteen base geologic units mapped from Voyager and Galileo observations. Colors distinguish interpreted plains, lava flows, patera floors and mountains. The separate diffuse-deposit overlay and structural linework are not shown. Gray grid marks unmapped or conflicting polygons; this view adds no measured relief.

spectral-slope.title: Sulfur-sensitive visible spectral slope
spectral-slope.summary: Sulfur-sensitive slope from 2° samples with approximate registration. Gray grid marks missing or withheld data; joins between nights remain. Values do not measure sulfur abundance.

visible-absorption.title: Continuum-relative visible absorption
visible-absorption.summary: A broad 520–660 nm absorption feature with uncertain chemical attribution. These 2° samples have approximate registration. Gray grid marks missing or withheld data; joins between nights remain.
